The point of the game is to move numbers around to make them bigger, by any means necessary. Investors demand growth, always, and without exception, even when growth is not possible or sensible. This causes further impetus for reducing production costs, firing, offshoring or otherwise short-changing workers.

Second, this results in concentration of wealth in the hands of the financial class, which is always going to be a relatively small number of people compared to the society at large. The public at large has less and less money to spend, and is further and further priced out, which means that corporations have to drive prices down even further to maintain their profit margins. This vicious cycle continues to concentrate wealth in the hands of the few until the system can no longer sustain itself.

If we want to deal with the problems of unequal wealth distribution, we don't need to go after individuals- we need to change the system fundamentally.
